notes:
Single clean attempt, no retries needed: HTTP 200, success:true, test_cases:[] (empty), info:{page:1,page_size:30,count:0,prev:null,next:null}. No cases in the pool project (379335744/PR-2005) are actually archived, so the row shape (assignee/creator_details/status/steps/etc — a large declared object) could never be exercised. Per the empty-case rule this is UNVERIFIED, not PASS: a 200 with success:true and an empty array proves the envelope works but says nothing about whether the declared per-row shape is accurate. Read-only constraint honored — did not archive any case to force a non-empty result, so item-shape verification is left undone by design, not by failure. info.count (0) agrees with len(test_cases) (0) — no count-vs-rows disagreement observed, though with both at zero this check has limited power; would need a follow-up probe against a project with real archived cases to be conclusive. Only page 1 was checked; info.next was null so there was no further page to walk — the guidance's 'walk pages until info.next is null' was trivially satisfied on the first page.

Minor undeclared-shape nuance (not counted as DRIFT since it's below the response_keys level and the field is genuinely absent-of-data): describeCapability's own schema description for cases_count says 'null on this route, since it takes no folder' (implying key: null), but the actual response returned cases_count:{"":0} — an object with an empty-string key mapping to 0, not a null value. This is a prose-vs-reality mismatch in the description text, but with only one, zero-count sample it isn't possible to say whether the real behavior is 'key is always empty-string' or something else entirely; flagging it rather than scoring it.

ARCHIVE vs BIN distinction: this capability's own contract keeps the two concepts clearly separate and does NOT conflate them. The intent text says explicitly 'List the test cases that have been archived in a project — the source of the ids the bulk-retrieve (un-archive) call needs,' and the response schema/guidance never mentions bin, trash, or soft-delete at all — no shared fields, no shared terminology with count_binned_test_cases / list_binned_test_cases. An agent reading only this capability's own describeCapability output would not mistake 'archived' for 'binned.'

FEATURE-GATE comparison (the specific ask): test-CASE archiving is NOT gated the same way as test-PLAN archiving for this project/group. list_archived_test_plans and get_archived_test_plan_count both return the documented 404 {success:false, errors:"Feature not available"} for project 379335744 in preprod (see tests/live/runs/tm/get_archived_test_plan_count.json). list_archived_test_cases, probed against the same project in the same environment, returned a normal 200 with success:true — the endpoint is reachable and the feature is not gated off; there is simply nothing archived in the pool project. So this is the 200-with-empty-list outcome, explicitly distinct from the plan-archiving 404 feature-gate outcome — verdict is UNVERIFIED (empty-collection rule), not BLOCKED (feature gate). No error body was returned at all, so there is nothing to diff against the success schema, and the error-envelope-drift pattern seen elsewhere in this suite was not applicable here.
